# runr_role (Resource)

A custom role of the organization (role-based access control). Give it to members (`runr members set-role`), groups (`runr_group.role`) or on single projects (`runr_project_access`). Built-in roles (owner, admin, developer, viewer) are part of RunR and cannot be managed. Needs `roles.manage`; nobody can create a role with permissions they do not hold themselves.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# A custom role: deploy and read logs and metrics, nothing else.
resource "runr_role" "release_manager" {
  name        = "Release manager"
  description = "Deploys releases and watches them"
  permissions = ["projects.deploy", "logs.view", "metrics.view"]
}

# effective_permissions lists them with the ones they imply (projects.view).
output "release_manager_permissions" {
  value = runr_role.release_manager.effective_permissions
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Display name.
- `permissions` (Set of String) Permissions of the role (`runr roles permissions` lists the catalog). The permissions they imply are added by RunR and listed in `effective_permissions`.

### Optional

- `description` (String) Description.
- `key` (String) Role key (letters, digits, `-`, `_`). Default: the slug of `name`. Changing it replaces the role.

### Read-Only

- `effective_permissions` (Set of String) `permissions` with every permission they imply (`env.edit` brings `env.view`).
- `id` (String) The role key.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# <role key> (custom roles only; `runr roles ls` lists the keys)
terraform import runr_role.release_manager release-manager
```
